title: Bosonization versus the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem
authors: Saif Ullah Baig, Shi Chen, Aleksey Cherman, Maria Neuzil
abstract: Thanks to bosonization, bosonic lattice models can offer a lattice regularization of chiral fermions. We construct chiral lattice fermion operators in the 2D modified Villain scalar model and evaluate their correlation functions. This microscopic bosonic model has an ultra-local action and an ultra-local symmetry that realizes the fermionic chiral symmetry under bosonization. The reconstructed lattice Dirac operator has no doublers, but is consistent with the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem because it turns out to be non-local. The non-locality of this derived quantity at finite lattice spacing does not pose any obstructions to gauging the non-anomalous symmetries of the model, which is itself ultra-local.
summary: This paper tackles the fundamental problem of regularizing chiral fermions on a lattice without violating symmetries. By employing bosonization within the 2D modified Villain model, the authors construct a doubler-free lattice Dirac operator that is non-local. This circumvents the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem's constraints by sacrificing locality while preserving the underlying symmetry structure.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is how to construct a lattice regularization for chiral fermions while preserving crucial symmetries, circumventing the constraints imposed by the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem.
main_result: The authors successfully constructed a doubler-free lattice Dirac operator using a bosonic approach that results in a non-local kernel, thereby bypassing the strict locality requirement of the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem.
method: The study employs bosonization techniques, utilizing the 2D modified Villain scalar model to relate an underlying ultra-local bosonic theory to the desired chiral fermionic description via path integral duality.
model_or_system: The focus is on the 2D modified Villain scalar model used to regularize chiral fermions. The analysis compares this bosonic formulation with continuum expectations for lattice Dirac operators, particularly in relation to chiral gauge theories.
key_observables: Correlation functions of constructed chiral lattice fermion operators; the structure and non-locality of the reconstructed lattice Dirac operator.
important_parameters: The dimensionality (2D), the specific form of the bosonic action (Villain model), and the finite lattice spacing ($a$).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that the underlying microscopic bosonic theory remains ultra-local, even if the derived fermionic operator is non-local at finite spacing.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail; notes refer to a 'Nielsen-Ninomiya scorecard' (Table I) and various correlation function comparisons on $S^2$ or $\mathbb{T}^2$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by reviewing the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem, introducing bosonization as an alternative regularization method, applying this to the 2D modified Villain model via duality arguments, and finally confirming the properties of the resulting lattice operator.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter/QFT, the techniques involving symmetry realization through bosonic dualities are highly relevant for understanding effective Hamiltonians in strongly correlated systems where continuum symmetries must be maintained on a lattice.
